Aggrieved by the dismissal of a petition filed, presumably under Section 358 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, (in short, 'BNSS'), to arraign the father-in-law and the mother-in-law of the petitioner as accused in C.C.No.244/2021 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Sasthamcotta, the de facto complainant in Crime No.1264/2021 of Sasthamcotta Police Station, has filed this petition under Section 528 BNSS with a prayer to direct the Trial Court to implead and summon the above persons, who are arraigned as respondents 3 & 4 in this petition.

2. On the basis of the complaint preferred by the petitioner, the Sasthamcotta Police registered a crime against her husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, on 30.08.2021.

However, while filing the final report, the Investigating Officer excluded the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the petitioner from the array of the accused, stating the reason that the investigation conducted did not reveal the involvement of the above accused in the crime.
Thus, the proceedings commenced against the husband of the de facto complainant alone in 2025:KER:58950 C.C.No.244/2021 before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Sasthamcotta.

sentences.text: After the examination of the de facto complainant as PW1, she filed a petition before the learned Magistrate with a prayer to proceed against her father-in-law and mother-in-law (respondents 3 & 4 in this petition) by issuing summons to them to answer the charge under Section 498A IPC.
By the impugned order dated 05.02.2025, the learned Magistrate dismissed the above petition.
Challenging the aforesaid order of the learned Magistrate, the petitioner is here before this Court with this petition.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the de facto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

4. In the First Information Statement (Annexure-A1) given by the de facto complainant to the S.I.
of Police Sasthamcotta, she had stated that her husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law had been subjecting her to cruelty demanding more dowry.
It was alleged that her father-in-law used to insist her to dispose of the landed property in her name for the purpose of purchasing a land at Ivarkala in the name of her husband.
She also alleged that her mother-in-law used to insult her, stating the inadequacy of the dowry which she brought at the time of her 2025:KER:58950 marriage with the first accused.

In addition to the above allegations, the de facto complainant had stated in Annexure-A1 that her father-in-law and mother-in-law tried to depict her as a woman of loose Anju Thompson vs State Of Kerala on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187223850/
2 morals.
5.

sentences.text: However, when examined before the Court as PW1, she did not state anything about the accusation in Annexure-A1 that her father-in-law and mother-in-law had tried to attribute unchastity and immorality upon her.
As per the testimony given by the petitioner as PW1, her father-in-law and mother-in-law often compelled her to dispose of her property and to purchase land in the name of her husband.
It is also stated that the petitioner's father-in-law and mother-in-law used to lament about the meagre dowry which she had brought.

Another statement which the petitioner had given before the learned Magistrate as PW1 is that during the pendency of a case for divorce before the Family Court, her husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law, along with church people and relatives, came to her house and demanded Rs.15,00,000/- to settle the issues.

It is on the basis of the aforesaid statements given by the de facto complainant before the learned Magistrate, that the respondents 3 & 4 are sought to be arraigned as additional accused in this case.

Going by the provisions contained in Section 358 BNSS, the requirement to be fulfilled for proceeding against persons who are not included as accused in the final report is that the enquiry or trial of the offence should disclose evidence pertaining to the commission of the offence by those persons sought to be arraigned as additional accused.

As far as the present case is concerned, it is not possible to say on the basis of the testimony of PW1 (Annexure-A3) before the learned Magistrate that the respondents 3 & 4 have committed the offence under Section 498A IPC.

A mere omnibus allegation that the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the petitioner used to insult her by demanding more dowry is not sufficient to fasten them with criminal liability under Section 498A IPC.

The statement given by the petitioner to the learned Magistrate at the time of her examination before the Court is not sufficient to show that the respondents 3 & 4 resorted to cruelty upon the petitioner.

Going by the contents of Section 498A IPC, the aforesaid offence would be attracted only in a case where there was wilful conduct of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to her life, limb or health, or harassment with a view to coerce her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security.

In the case on 2025:KER:58950 hand, the statement given by PW1 does not contain the requisite particulars to bring home the wilful conduct or harassment of the nature envisaged under Section 498A IPC.

A casual, vague and superficial allegation that the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the petitioner insisted and quarrelled for bringing more dowry by the petitioner and also to sell the property standing in her name for the purchase of land in the name of her husband, cannot be termed as evidence pointing to the cruelty envisaged under Section 498A IPC.

In that view of the matter, the learned Magistrate cannot be found to be at fault for dismissing the petition filed by the petitioner for proceeding against her father-in-law and mother-in-law for the commission of the above offence.
Needless to say that the present petition is devoid of merits.
In the result, the petition is hereby dismissed.
